entities.summary: Solomonia Yuryevna Saburova was the grand princess of Moscow as the wife of Vasili III of Russia. Born into a noble family, she rose to prominence through her strategic marriages and political acumen. In 1480, Saburova married Vasili III, who became the Grand Prince of Moscow, and she played a crucial role in securing the alliance between Moscow and the Tver principality. Their marriage produced two children, including the future Vasili IV, who succeeded his father as Grand Prince. Saburova's influence extended beyond her role as a queen, as she oversaw the development of the Moscow Kremlin and promoted the arts, including the construction of the Trinity Church. Her legacy continued after her death in 1542, as she was canonized by the Russian Orthodox Church as Saint Sofia of Suzdal. The saint's feast day, celebrated on December 28, remains a significant date in the Russian Orthodox calendar. Saburova's contributions to the cultural and political landscape of 16th-century Russia have been recognized by historians as a testament to her intelligence, diplomacy, and devotion to her family and faith.
